answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before earning, and peers can slash that stake when they prove misbehavior. Think of the deposit as an opal, costly to replace, while a clean history grows like a pearl, layer by layer, earning trust slowly. A newcomer starts at ferrous-grade access, limited to small tasks until attested work proves reliability. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand deposits, and every Sybil that misbehaves forfeits its bond, so attack cost scales linearly while the payoff stays capped.
